subject: Reusing compiled nimbleFunctions between R sessions

messages.author: 2b032b0e04c3c0cf
messages.subject: Reusing compiled nimbleFunctions between R sessions
parts:
Is there a way to reuse a compiled `nimbleFunction` between different R sessions? `compileNimble` generates the code, compiles it, and then loads the compiled objects. It looks like it creates a file (such as a .dll in windows) in a temporary directory for this. In theory this file could be reused in a new session, such that it would not have to be compiled again if there were no changes to the code. Is this possible? The main purpose I'd like to do this is to use a compiled nimbleFunction in my own custom package. If it was possible to do this I could use the .onLoad function to check if the compiled file exists, then load that, or otherwise compile the nimbleFunction. Therefore the function would only have to be compiled once, when the user loads the package for the first time. At the moment I compile the function when the package is loaded every time, but this adds a small but annoying extra amount of time for loading the package. I've tried saving the resulting returned object from compileNimble into an .rds file and then loading that, but this doesn't work most of the time, presumably because it seems to be dependent on a symbol in the nimble environment (or something like that)? I'm new to writing R packages, so I haven't got all of this stuff down yet.
I'd appreciate any thoughts on this issue. 

Thanks,

Russell

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Reusing compiled nimbleFunctions between R sessions
parts:
Hi Russell,

This is something we’ve been wanting to make possible, but it has fallen below other priorities and so remains not done.  Now that you are asking, we can try to kick it up the list.  

By the way, you can control where the code and dll are put using the dirName argument to compileNimble.  If you use dirName = ‘.’, they will go in your current working directory.

Is it a nimbleFunction that does not have setup code?  If so, I could set up a quick way for you to do it before we have a more friendly version implemented.  I think all one would need is to use R CMD SHLIB to compile the generated C++ and modify the first argument to .Call in the R function returned by compileNimble to call the loaded dll.

If you eventually want to submit your package to CRAN, we’ll have to work out how to compile with nimble’s headers during CRAN package building.

Perry

messages.subject: Re: Reusing compiled nimbleFunctions between R sessions
parts:
Hi Perry,

Thanks for your prompt reply. As a matter of fact it is a nimbleFunction without setup code. So I would appreciate any sort of hack that would allow me to reuse the compiled code in my package.
Thanks for the dirName option tip. I had noted that option in the help, but it only mentioned that is where it would put the C++ code, but of course it makes sense that the dll would also go there.
As far as CRAN goes, that may be a consideration for the future, but at the moment I only intend to distribute the package via github. 

And by the way, just wanted to say, nimble is a fantastic package! Thanks for all your and the development team's hard work on it. I've already used it extensively for several projects. So I'm definitely interested in any developments in terms of helping to integrate nimble into other packages, as I have plans for several that would use nimble functionality.

Cheers,
Russell
